newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Only oil shares brighten dull Nigerian market.
newsitem.headline: Only oil shares brighten dull Nigerian market.

text.p: Shares of many of Nigeria's biggest companies were hit by profit-taking, with only the oil marketing sector showing significant gains in slow Friday trade.
The all-share index closed at 6,972.20 from 6,971.39 on Thursday.
Unipetrol gained 25 kobo to 57.75 naira, Total added 15 kobo to 57.15 naira. National Oil went up 13 kobo to 46.63 naira and Mobil finished 10 kobo higher at 49.60 naira.
Outside the oil sector West African Portland Cement Company climbed 70 kobo to 46.00 naira while other cement companies fell.
Conglomerate Lever Brothers dropped 10 kobo to 20.40 naira. Tyre-makers Dunlop was 20 kobo down at 8.20 naira. Nigerian Breweries finished five kobo lower at 19.40 naira.
Afribank closed 20 kobo down at 3.80 naira while Guaranty Trust Bank fell five kobo to 11.40 naira.
Traders said slow trading would remain to the end of the year as brokerage houses closed up shop for the Christmas holiday.
